attempted_claim: Let F be a number field, n>=3, n'>=1, and fix pi' in F_{n'} and small eps>0. Let F_n(Q)={pi : C_pi<=Q}. Prove, unconditionally and with effectively computable constants, that there exist c=c(n,n',[F:Q],eps)>0, A=A(n,n')>0 and eta=eta(n,n',[F:Q],eps)>0 such that for all large Q, for all pi in F_n(Q) outside an exceptional set E(Q) with |E(Q)| <<_{F,n,n',pi',eps} |F_n(Q)|^{1-eta}, and for every chi in F_1 with C(chi)<=Q^A, L(sigma,pi x (pi' otimes chi)) != 0 for sigma >= 1-c*(C(pi)C(pi')C(chi))^{-eps}, with no exceptional character psi_{pi,pi',eps} and no ineffectivity: the constant c is effective and the same c works for all non-exceptional pi and all chi in range. In particular the single possibly-ineffective Harcos-Thorner twist is shown to carry no Siegel zero for almost all pi, by coupling the Goldfeld-Hoffstein-Lieman lower-bound mechanism to the GRC-independent pre-sifted large sieve for L^{-1} and log L with ramified-place control. The claim is asymptotic in Q->infinity (pi' fixed), unconditional, and effective; no GRH/GRC assumption and no individual (all-pi) standard region is asserted.
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the target was obtained: no Siegel zero was exhibited and no effective no-exception strip was established. The work documents three concrete blocked routes and one bounded computation; it does not supply the missing effective chi-uniform L(1) bound or the GRC-independent ramified sieve, and it claims no emergent theorem.
